analyzed_vuln.description: Heap OOB write is caused by undersized edge emulation scratch buffer allocation. get_buffer() allocates s->edge_emu_buffer as av_calloc(pic->f->linesize[0], 17), i.e. exactly 17 luma lines. But svq3_mc_dir_part() calls emulated_edge_mc() for both luma and chroma with block_h = height+1 and writes up to block_h rows at buf_linesize stride. For luma 16x16 MC, block_h becomes 17 and exactly fits; for chroma after subsampling, width/height are halved but blocksize can still require edge emulation and the same shared buffer is reused with uvlinesize stride and right-edge fill loop writes to index end_x..block_w-1. With crafted motion vectors near borders, ff_emulated_edge_mc_8 writes one byte past the 17*linesize allocation (ASan shows write at buffer end). Root cause is missing size validation/incorrect sizing contract in get_buffer for all emulated_edge_mc call patterns, not in ff_emulated_edge_mc itself.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Trigger via SVQ3 bitstream that reaches inter/B-frame motion compensation (svq3_decode_mb -> svq3_mc_dir -> svq3_mc_dir_part) with motion vectors clipped to border so emu=1. Decoder then calls vdsp.emulated_edge_mc on s->edge_emu_buffer. Because buffer is allocated once with fixed 17*linesize[0] bytes and reused for multiple planes/strides, crafted border MC parameters lead to ff_emulated_edge_mc_8 right-edge replication writing past the heap chunk end. PoC drives this path through ffmpeg_AV_CODEC_ID_SVQ3_fuzzer input.
